title: Mercy, not sacrifice (Matthew 9:1–13)
hookLine: go and learn what this means, quoting Hosea 6:6
tomorrow: what happens when two people need him at once?

cards: Mid-argument in a comment section, someone types: read the actual article first. Matthew's version comes at a dinner.
Jesus has called a man from the tax booth with two words, follow me, and the man "arose, and followed him." Now the table fills with tax collectors and people the town calls sinners.
Some Pharisees, teachers devoted to keeping God's law, ask the disciples a real question: "Why eateth your Master with publicans and sinners?" Jesus answers with homework.

teach.b: "They that be whole need not a physician, but they that are sick. But go ye and learn what that meaneth, I will have mercy, and not sacrifice."
Go and learn sends people back to a text they already share: the prophet Hosea, scripture for Jesus and the Pharisees alike.
"For I desired mercy, and not sacrifice; and the knowledge of God more than burnt offerings." So this is an argument inside one Bible about what it puts first.
Christians read the line two ways, and both deserve a hearing.
One view hears instead of: what God wants is kindness, not ceremony, and any rule that keeps the sick from the doctor has missed the point.
The other view hears more than: look at Hosea's second half, the knowledge of God more than burnt offerings. That's a ranking, not a ban.
Worship stays; mercy goes first. The first view asks: what's a ritual worth if it shuts someone out? The second answers: the same scripture asks for both, in the right order.
Both agree on the table. Matthew even opens the page with a man on a bed hearing, "Son, be of good cheer; thy sins be forgiven thee." Mercy comes first in both scenes.

how: Some Christians use Hosea 6:6 when they examine their conscience, and churches that keep a calendar of saints read the calling of Matthew on his feast day.

games.q: you've always heard mercy, not sacrifice as mercy instead of worship. state the other reading at its strongest.
o: Hosea's next words, more than burnt offerings, rank them: mercy first, worship kept.
sacrifice meant giving up treats, so Jesus says skip self-denial.
mercy is for strangers, and sacrifice is for your own family.

practice: Name one disagreement where being right has started to matter more than the person.
Picture the obstacle, the line you always want to win with; then choose one plain, merciful move for the next time it comes up, and hold it as you breathe.
